class: a propagated verdict nothing caused, and the history a forger builds to hide it

expect.why: the ground has not moved, so the verdict discharges a finding that was never made; it records the digest the anchor itself names, which states no drift

commit 03 really does move the ground, and the verdict written at commit 02 does not describe that drift: it records the digest the anchor names, which is not what this run reads the section as. A verdict matched to a ground by its pointer alone silenced this flag, which is how a discharge carrying any value at all — or none — kept a real, committed, ongoing drift at exit 0
the refutable half is asked of every pointer whether or not its ground is fresh: the record states no drift whatever the tree does afterwards, and a real drift on top of it does not launder it

commit 03 edits the artifact and commit 04 puts it back, so every commit since the pin has touched it — and the ground is byte-identical to the pin throughout. Asked whether the artifact was ever touched, an earlier rule read that as proof the discharge was caused and accepted it permanently; asked of history at all, a later one could be handed a version the path really held. Nothing is asked of history now: the record is the digest the anchor itself names, which states no drift, so it is still an orphan

history: apply commits/01, commits/02, … as successive commits in a fresh repository; expectations name the commit they apply to. `@commitNN` in an entry is substituted with the real short object id of that commit before it is made, because a seed cannot know an id the runner has not created yet
